newsitem.title: FRANCE: French minister revives U.S. "snub" incident.
newsitem.headline: French minister revives U.S. "snub" incident.

text.p: French Foreign Minister Herve de Charette revived on Wednesday a controversy over a purported snub to U.S. Secretary of State Warren Christopher, saying it had been created and manipulated by "American circles".

"It was a grotesque incident but it was entirely manipulated by American circles who were at its origin," a furious de Charette told parliament after a senior opposition politician poured scorn on him by to the merriment, or anger, of the house. The minister did not elaborate.
The dispute arose when, according to U.S. officials, de Charette walked out during a toast in honour of Christopher at a NATO function in Brussels earlier this month.
The French minister's office said he had not meant to snub Christopher and a French official said he left because he did not know a tribute to the secretary of state would be delivered.
De Charette and Christopher have since met and both sides said they had put the matter behind them.
But Socialist Paul Quiles, a former defence minister, reopened the wound when he told de Charette in parliament that his prestige came out "in tatters from this ridiculous incident."

He also said that under de Charette's leadership, France had become an object of international ridicule, the Americans "were masters of the world" and French efforts to gain more influence in NATO were doomed to failure.

"I find it extremely odd you come here to plead the cause of those (U.S.) circles. We should both be defending France's respectability. I am shocked to see you mocking French foreign policy. What you have said is pathetic," de Charette responded as the assembly broke into uproar.
The alleged snub in Brussels followed a series of disputes between Paris and Washington including the question of who should hold NATO's southern command based in Naples.
